page: Amazon Web Services r8a.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with a single dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 core operating at up to 4.5 GHz with one thread. Memory is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no local storage and relies on network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and zero bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded processing capabilities alongside the expected throughput constraints of a single-core environment. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing (2790.0) and stress-ng single-core performance (3753.98), accompanied by fast single-threaded gzip compression at 41.09 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput ranks in the lower percentiles across PassMark CPU (3479.37) and Clang software compilation (2775.0) due to the single vCPU allocation. Memory throughput reaches 46.87 GB/sec for uncached reads and 34.48 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, r8a.medium provides an entry point to DDR5 memory channels and modern Zen-based AMD architecture without requiring multi-core commitments. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage and high-bandwidth networking limits its profile for intensive storage pipelines. The instance is suited for lightweight memory-bound utilities, small in-memory caching nodes, single-threaded processing daemons, and low-traffic web services that require dedicated CPU clock consistency paired with an 8 GB memory footprint.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.medium is a memory-optimized instance featuring one dedicated x86_64 vCPU derived from an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it is configured with 8.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The hardware profile does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached volumes, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-decile single-core CPU and compression metrics, balanced by entry-level multi-core throughput due to the single-thread execution model. Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 46.87 GB/sec read and 34.48 GB/sec write bandwidth. The r8a.medium is suited for small-scale memory-intensive workloads, single-threaded data tasks, lightweight caching, and development services.
